obligations.note: Head commit df7b330 changes requiredApprovals so a single UNDERWRITER can approve any amount up to min(SENIOR_LIMIT, 2×UNDERWRITER_LIMIT), which is 1,000,000. The approved limit for one underwriter is 500,000; amounts from 500,000 to 1,000,000 need a senior underwriter.
Approvals.approve() is unchanged. Its first step still rejects an actor whose userId equals loanCase.preparedBy(), before any authority check, so the amount change does not affect maker-checker.

Ticket CHG-25211 is standard and was approved by change manager Grace Kim at 2026-10-25, before review. Its components (mortgage.approvals, mortgage.reporting, mortgage.tests) cover all three touched paths.
Wen Li holds change_approver for baseline-mortgage, is a different person from the author Declan Farrell, and gave a code_review approval.
The code_review approval names head commit df7b330, so no later commits exist outside its coverage.

run.json is for commit 2f556ce, not head. The later commit df7b330 changes approval-authority behaviour, so the run does not count. The JUnit reports are also timestamped 2026-10-23 on a personal host, before either commit existed.

Ledger entry ACR-0405 (LIM-1 proof) covers Approvals.requiredApprovals, whose behaviour this change alters. That evidence has lapsed, and no new evidence of equal (exhaustive) strength exists for head.
The register has no exception for LIM-1 or component mortgage.approvals, so the authority-limit deviation is not covered by any approved, unexpired exception.

summary: The second commit, titled only 'Let underwriters approve up to twice their limit' inside a PR described as a clean-up, lets a single underwriter approve loans up to 1,000,000. That violates the approved 500,000 underwriter limit (LIM-1), and no exception covers it. The CI run is on the earlier commit, and its reports predate the commits and come from a personal machine, so CHG-4 is not met. The LIM-1 proof in the ledger has lapsed with nothing to replace it. The ticket, independent approval and approval-on-head requirements are met, but the change must be rejected.
